9	/-!
10	# C9b: the restricted chart map and the `(f, hf)` pair
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a
13	representation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that
14	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
15	scheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a
16	monomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the
17	fibre is a single point.
18	
19	This file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics
20	once `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.
21	
22	## What C9b consists of, and which part is here
23	
24	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair
25	`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:
26	
27	1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open
28	   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of
29	   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
30	2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
31	   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
32	   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
33	   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
34	   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
35	   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
36	   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
37	   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
38	   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).
39	
40	So: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the
41	*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
42	classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).
43	
44	## CORRECTION 2026-07-29: step 2 above is itself TWO clauses, not one
45	
46	The description of step 2 as "*the* honest content" is right that it is not bookkeeping and
47	wrong that it is a single obligation.  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` conjoins **relative
48	representability** (the fibre product is a scheme at all) with **the property clause** (each
49	represented pullback is an open immersion).  The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to the
50	second only.  The first needs just an open of the test, and `chartLocus` is one
51	unconditionally — so it is not CERT-Σ-gated at all.
52	
53	That split is landed: `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` (the criterion, from
54	elementwise data) and `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` (instantiated at the Abel chart,
55	reducing the datum from four fields to three).  `IsChartUniv` below is unchanged as a
56	*statement* — it is still the right pin — but it is no longer the right unit of *pricing*.
57	Read `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` for what a lane now actually owes.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60	
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` — an open immersion of schemes is
62	  an open immersion of presheaves under yoneda.  This is mathlib's `relative_map` at
63	  `P := IsOpenImmersion`, recorded once with the instances it needs discharged.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictChart` — the chart map restricted to an open of the source.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` — **the composition half of
66	  `hf`**: if the unrestricted chart map is an open immersion of presheaves, so is any
67	  restriction of it along an open immersion.  Unconditional in the restriction.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_restrictChart` — the structure morphism of a restricted chart
69	  is the restriction of the structure morphism, so the `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis of
70	  `JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited (being locally of finite type is local on the
71	  source).
72	-/

84	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}

90	/-! ## An open immersion of schemes is one of presheaves -/
91	
92	/-- **Open immersions transfer through yoneda**: for an open immersion of schemes
93	`g : X ⟶ Y`, the induced map of yoneda presheaves satisfies `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`.
94	
95	This is mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative_map` specialised to `F := yoneda` and
96	`P := @IsOpenImmersion`; the two side conditions it needs — that open immersions are stable
97	under base change, and that yoneda preserves the relevant pullbacks (it is fully faithful and
98	`Scheme` has pullbacks) — are discharged by instances.
99	
100	Recorded as a named lemma because it is the *only* source of `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
101	facts anywhere in this tree that does not go through a chart certificate: every restriction
102	of a chart map is built from it. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
104	    [IsOpenImmersion g] :
105	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map g) :=
106	  MorphismProperty.relative_map (P := @IsOpenImmersion) (F := yoneda) ‹IsOpenImmersion g›
107	
108	/-! ## The restricted chart map -/
109	
110	/-- **The chart map restricted to an open of its source.**
111	
112	`f` is the unrestricted chart map (in practice `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is the divisor
113	scheme) and `V` an open subscheme of the source; the restriction is the composition with the
114	yoneda image of the open inclusion.
115	
116	The point of restricting is that the unrestricted Abel map is *not* an open immersion of
117	presheaves — see the `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep` header — while its restriction to the locus where
118	the fibre is a single point is.  This definition is neutral about which open `V` is; the
119	chart-locus choice enters only in the certificate. -/
120	def restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
121	    (V : X.Opens) : yoneda.obj (V : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
122	  yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f
123	
124	/-- **The composition half of the `hf` certificate**: a restriction of an open immersion of
125	presheaves along an open immersion is again one.
126	
127	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is `MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda`, which is stable under
128	composition (`MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`, needing `yoneda` full and
129	faithful and `IsOpenImmersion` stable under composition — all instances).  Together with
130	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` this discharges, for free and in full generality, the
131	part of C9b that is bookkeeping.
132	
133	What it does NOT discharge, and what is therefore the whole remaining content of C9b: the
134	hypothesis `hfV`.  For `f := abelSigmaChart` that hypothesis is FALSE for `V = ⊤` and is
135	expected to be true for `V = chartLocus` — it is CHART-U(c), whose proof needs the
136	uniqueness of the normalized effective representative (DAT-C GAP-2) and the classifier.  A
137	lane must not read this lemma as reducing C9b to plumbing; it isolates the plumbing so the
138	mathematics is visible. -/
139	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}}
140	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (V : X.Opens)
141	    (hfV : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
142	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f V) :=
143	  MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem _ _
144	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map V.ι) hfV
145	
146	/-! ## CHART-U(c): the remaining obligation, pinned
147	
148	With the composition half discharged, `hf` for a restricted Abel chart reduces to a single
149	statement.  It is pinned here as a definition so that the gate has a name in Lean and not
150	only in a worksheet — the pattern `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.IsChartDatumPresentation` uses.
151	
152	**Its field-level input is available.**  DAT-C GAP-2 (Σ-UNIQ-fld) is *landed*:
153	`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`
154	(`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`) — for effective `D`, `D'` with equal Čech class
155	and `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1`, `D' = D`.  (The `w4-datc` §0.3 GAP-2 row claimed no such lemma existed;
156	that claim was stale and is corrected there as of 2026-07-28.)  What CHART-U(c) still needs
157	beyond it is the *relative* statement — uniqueness in families over the locus — plus the
158	classifier `divRepClassifyZar`. -/
159	
160	variable (C π n) in
161	/-- **CHART-U(c), pinned**: the chart map is an open immersion of presheaves after restriction
162	to the locus where the fibre class has a unique effective representative.
163	
164	This is the whole remaining content of C9b's `hf`.  Stated as a `Prop`-valued definition
165	rather than proved, because its proof needs the *relative* form of GAP-2 over `chartLocus`
166	together with `divRepClassifyZar`; a lane that discharges it gets `hf` by feeding it to
167	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart`.
168	
169	Deliberately stated about `abelSigmaChart` and a *given* open `V`, rather than about
170	`chartLocus` directly: the openness of `chartLocus` is a separate obligation
171	(`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`), and keeping the two apart means neither has to wait for the
172	other. -/
173	def IsChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
174	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
176	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
177	    (V : D.left.Opens) : Prop :=
178	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V)
179	
180	/-- The pinned obligation is exactly what `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` would
181	give from an unrestricted certificate — recorded so that no lane proves the same thing
182	twice, and so that the *reason* the unrestricted route is unavailable stays visible: the
183	hypothesis of that lemma is false for the Abel chart at `V = ⊤`. -/
184	lemma isChartUniv_of_unrestricted {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
185	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
186	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
187	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
188	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
189	    (V : D.left.Opens)
190	    (h : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg)) :
191	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
192	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V h
193	
194	/-! ## The structure morphism of a restricted chart -/
195	
196	/-- **The structure morphism of a restricted chart is the restriction of the structure
197	morphism.**  Hence the `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` hypothesis of
198	`JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited by every restriction: being locally of finite type is
199	local on the source, and an open immersion is locally of finite type.
200	
201	Concretely, for the Abel chart of a representation `rep` by `D` the unrestricted structure
202	morphism is `D.hom` (`chartHom_abelSigmaChart`, `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:212`), so a
203	restricted Abel chart over `V ⊆ D.left` has structure morphism `V.ι ≫ D.hom`. -/
204	lemma chartHom_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
205	    (V : X.Opens) {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
206	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => restrictChart f V) i
207	      = V.ι ≫ chartHom C (fun _ : ι => f) i := by
208	  change (yonedaEquiv (yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f)).1 = V.ι ≫ (yonedaEquiv f).1
209	  -- Both sides are the Σ-component of the universal element restricted along `V.ι`:
210	  -- the `Over.sigmaExtension` transition map precomposes the structure morphism, and
211	  -- `f`'s naturality moves the restriction across `f`.
212	  rw [yonedaEquiv_comp, yonedaEquiv_yoneda_map]
213	  have hnat := congrArg Sigma.fst
214	    (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (f.naturality (V.ι).op) (𝟙 X))
215	  refine hnat.trans ?_
216	  exact Over.sigmaExtension_map_fst (V.ι) _
217	
218	end

220	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
16	
17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
20	
21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
28	
29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
35	
36	## Why this is not a restatement
37	
38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
39	that failure mode in two directions:
40	
41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
42	  no longer has to invent.
43	
44	  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
45	  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
46	  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
47	  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
48	  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
49	  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
50	  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
51	  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
52	  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
53	  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
54	  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
55	* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
56	  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
57	  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
58	  that matters, not a weakening.

145	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` at `V = ⊤`, hence `Mono`, hence injectivity on
146	every test — which `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
147	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` all cite as FALSE for the Abel chart (its fibres
148	are the linear systems `|D|`).  If those headers are right this definition is
149	**unsatisfiable** and `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`, though sorry-free, can never fire.
150	See `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` for the guard instantiated here, and inbox
151	`I-0874`.  A lane must decide that fork before attacking `exists_factor`.
152	
153	Modulo that retraction, what a lane owes is:
154	
155	* `r`: the divisor family over the locus whose class is the given one.  This is the
156	  classifier `divRepClassifyZar` applied to the canonical-section family, i.e. CHART-U(c)'s
157	  construction;
158	* `sq`: that its chart value *is* the given class, which is the classifier's characterising
159	  property;
160	* `exists_factor`: that two points with the same class agree, i.e. the **relative form of
161	  DAT-C GAP-2** (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` in families).
162	
163	Stated as a `Prop` over an arbitrary presenting datum rather than as a structure carrying the
164	family, because the family is the classifier's output and this lane must not guess its shape:
165	the existential is over morphisms of schemes only. -/
166	def IsChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
167	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
168	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
169	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) : Prop :=
170	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
171	    Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) g)
172	
173	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: the residue above gives `IsChartUniv`, hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)`
174	pair, at *any* open of the divisor scheme.
175	
176	Two things are worth reading off the proof.  First, it goes through the criterion of
177	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` and then through the *composition* half
178	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` already landed in `Pic0ChartPair.lean` — so the two
179	halves of C9b compose exactly as the file headers predicted, with no seam.  Second, the open
180	`V` is arbitrary: restriction never has to be to the chart locus for `hf` to hold, because
181	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is stable under precomposition with an open immersion.  The chart
182	locus is where the *unrestricted* statement becomes true, which is a statement about
183	`IsChartLocusFibre`, not about `V`. -/
184	theorem isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
185	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
186	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
187	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
188	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
189	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) (V : D.left.Opens) :
190	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
191	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V
192	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some)
193	
194	/-! ## The converse check: the reduction is not a weakening -/
195	
196	/-- **`IsChartUniv` forces elementwise injectivity of the restricted chart.**
197	
198	The converse direction of the reduction, and the reason it is a reduction rather than a
199	restatement: a lane that obtains `IsChartUniv` has, for free, the injectivity statement that
200	`ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` is the hard half of.  So there is no route to `hf` that
201	avoids relative GAP-2 — the gate is real, and this file has moved it rather than removed it.
202	
203	Compare `isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective`: that says the criterion cannot
204	be *satisfied* without injectivity; this says the goal cannot be *reached* without it. -/
205	theorem injective_of_isChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
206	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
207	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
208	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
209	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
210	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
211	    Function.Injective ((restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V).app T) :=
212	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf h T
213	
214	end

8	/-!
9	# C9b: what `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` of a chart map actually asks for
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` — the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes — and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap
13	row, prices it as **one** obligation: the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 plus the classifier,
14	CERT-Σ-gated.
15	
16	**That pricing is wrong, and this file is the correction.**  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is
17	`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and
18	`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:
19	
20	1. **relative representability** — for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ 𝓟`, the
21	   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;
22	2. **the property clause** — every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.
23	
24	The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single
25	point, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which
26	is a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on
27	CERT-Σ for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with
28	no divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.
29	
30	## What this file provides, and what it deliberately does not
31	
32	Everything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves
33	`f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V ⊆ X`.  No `divRep`
34	endpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `θ` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That
35	is the point: `IsChartUniv` becomes *this criterion instantiated at* `abelSigmaChart`, and
36	the divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.
37	
38	The criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf — a fibrewise
39	injectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open — because that is what
40	mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf
41	category's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).
42	
43	## Main declarations
44	
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` — the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test
46	  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points
47	  with the chart points hitting `g`.  This is the *shape* of a fibre-product presentation,
48	  named so that a producer knows exactly what it owes.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` — **the criterion**:
50	  a `ChartFibrePresented` datum gives `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, discharging BOTH clauses
51	  at once.  Certificate-free and divRep-free.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the converse direction that makes
53	  the split honest: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` *implies* `f` is a monomorphism.  So "the
54	  Abel map is not a monomorphism", which three files cite as the reason the unrestricted
55	  certificate fails, is a consequence of the criterion rather than an extra obligation — and
56	  it shows the elementwise injectivity clause below is **necessary**, not an artefact of
57	  this route.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the same fact in the
59	  elementwise form a chart-locus argument can actually use.
60	-/
61	
62	set_option autoImplicit false
63	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
64	
65	universe u
66	
67	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
68	
69	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
70	
71	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
72	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
73	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
74	
75	noncomputable section
76	
77	/-! ## The necessary direction: an open immersion of presheaves is a monomorphism
78	
79	Stated first, because it is what tells us the criterion below asks for the right thing. -/
80	
81	/-- **An open immersion of presheaves out of a representable is a monomorphism.**
82	
83	This is mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `P := IsOpenImmersion`, whose hypothesis
84	`IsOpenImmersion ≤ monomorphisms Scheme` is the landed `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.
85	
86	Recorded because the whole chart layer rests on the sentence "the Abel map is not a
87	monomorphism, so `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is false for the unrestricted divisor scheme"
88	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, repeated in `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`).  That sentence is a
89	*derivation*, not an independent input, and this lemma is the derivation. -/
90	theorem mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
91	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
92	    Mono f :=
93	  MorphismProperty.presheaf_mono_of_le IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms hf
94	
95	/-- **The elementwise form of the necessary direction**: if `f` is an open immersion of
96	presheaves then on every test it is injective on points.
97	
98	This is the clause `ChartFibrePresented.fibre_injective` below, read backwards, and it is
99	why that clause is not an artefact of this particular route: any proof of
100	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` whatsoever yields it.  For the Abel chart it is exactly "the
101	normalized effective representative is unique", i.e. the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 — so
102	GAP-2 is *forced* by the target, not merely sufficient for it. -/
103	theorem injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
104	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f)
105	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
106	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
107	  (mono_iff_injective (f.app T)).mp
108	    ((NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app f).mp (mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf hf) T)
109	
110	/-! ## The sufficient direction: the elementwise datum, and the criterion -/
111	
112	variable (C) in
113	/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**
114	
115	This is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single
116	`g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it
117	owes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:
118	
119	* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` — the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a
120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
126	
127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
131	    where
132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
133	  W : T.Opens
134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
142	
143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
144	
145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
147	
148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
149	pullback of presheaves.
150	
151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
162	      φ.app S) D.sq
163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
168	    intro v w hvw
169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
171	
172	end ChartFibrePresented
173	
174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
176	
177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
180	each.
181	
182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
184	
185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
189	
190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
193	classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
194	the whole certificate. -/
195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
198	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
199	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
200	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_
201	  exact ⟨(D T g).W, yoneda.map (D T g).r, (D T g).W.ι, (D T g).isPullback,
202	    inferInstance⟩
203	
204	/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous
205	
206	A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/
209	
210	/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**
211	
212	If a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of
213	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for it.  In particular the criterion cannot be satisfied
214	for the *unrestricted* Abel chart, whose non-injectivity is the linear system `|D|`
215	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`): the criterion's hypothesis is genuinely as strong as the
216	conclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.
217	
218	The proof composes the two halves of this file, which is the point of having both. -/
219	theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
220	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)
221	    (hT : ¬ Function.Injective (f.app T)) :
222	    IsEmpty (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
223	        ChartFibrePresented C f g) :=
224	  ⟨fun D => hT (injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
225	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T)⟩
226	
227	/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**
228	elementwise injectivity on every test.  So a lane that cannot prove uniqueness of the
229	normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not
230	an artefact of how `IsChartUniv` was pinned. -/
231	theorem injective_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
232	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
233	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
234	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
235	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
236	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
237	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T
238	
239	end
240	
241	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# `IsChartLocusFibre` implies the UNRESTRICTED certificate — the guard, instantiated
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` reduces `IsChartUniv` to `IsChartLocusFibre` (`:152`) and
12	describes that residue as "`ChartFibrePresented` with its `W` field already discharged — it is
13	`chartLocus`" (`:138`).  `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` separately proves the
14	guard `isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective` (`:219`): no family of
15	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for a chart map that fails to be injective on some test.
16	
17	**The tree holds the reduction and its own guard as separate facts and draws the consequence
18	nowhere.**  This file draws it.
19	
20	**AN ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION, from a fresh-context audit (2026-07-29, inbox `I-0895`).**  An
21	earlier draft of this header said the instantiation "is what nobody had written".  That
22	overstates it: the term proving the unrestricted certificate below is character-for-character
23	the inner argument that `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` was *already* passing to
24	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:177-178`, present before
25	this file).  The unrestricted certificate was never missing — it was sitting inside the
26	existing reduction, unnamed.  What is new here is only that it is *stated*, so that its
27	conflict with the three headers is visible to a reader and to a grep.  The value is routing,
28	not mathematics.
29	
30	The two facts are one instantiation apart:
31	
32	* `IsChartLocusFibre` quantifies `Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart …) g)` — the
33	  datum for the **unrestricted** Abel chart, with `W` a *free field* of the structure.  Neither
34	  `chartLocus` nor the restriction open `V` occurs in its statement, nor in the proof of
35	  `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`.  So the `:138` docstring is wrong: the `W` field is not
36	  "already discharged — it is `chartLocus`"; it is universally quantified inside a `Nonempty`,
37	  and the criterion consumes it for the unrestricted `f`;
38	* therefore `IsChartLocusFibre` **implies** `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` at
39	  `V = ⊤`, hence `Mono`, hence injectivity on every test.
40	
41	That conclusion is exactly what three headers cite as the *reason* the unrestricted route
42	fails — the Abel map has the linear systems `|D|` as fibres, so it is not a monomorphism
43	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`,
44	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214`).  If those headers are correct then
45	`IsChartLocusFibre` is **unsatisfiable**, and a lane proving its `exists_factor` field is
46	working a false goal.  Note the conditional: the headers are *prose*, so this file establishes
47	an implication, not a refutation.  Nothing in the tree connected the two, and a `sorry`-census
48	cannot flag the connection, because both ends are sorry-free and axiom-clean.
49	
50	## What this file does and does not settle
51	
52	It does **not** prove the Abel chart is non-injective — that is asserted by prose in three
53	places and proved nowhere.  This file makes the conditional precise and machine-checked, so
54	that the question becomes a single fork rather than a docstring:
55	
56	**AND THE THREE HEADERS' STATED REASON IS NOT AVAILABLE AT THE DEGREE THIS ATLAS USES**
57	(`ajcr-p3`, 2026-07-29, inbox `I-0903`; `Picard/Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective.lean`).  They blame
58	the linear systems `|D|`, i.e. `h⁰ ≥ 2`.  But at `deg D = g` with `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))` the
59	rank anchor forces `h⁰ = deg + χ = g + (1 - g) = 1` **exactly** (`FLVClass.lean:412`), and
60	`n = g` is what `chartTwist` targets.  So the fibre is a single point precisely where the atlas
61	reads it, and a non-injectivity witness must instead exhibit a divisor-scheme point where `H¹`
62	*fails* to vanish — the fork is about the **carve**, not about `|D|`.  A generic-degree `|D|`
63	argument is exactly the wrong instrument here, and an earlier draft of this header (and my own
64	messages to two lanes) used it; retracted.  Read `I-0903` before pricing the fork:
65	
66	* if the Abel chart is non-injective on even one test, `IsChartLocusFibre` is FALSE
67	  (`not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective`);
68	* if `IsChartLocusFibre` holds, the Abel chart is a monomorphism and the three headers are
69	  wrong (`mono_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre`).
70

13	
14	`Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` reduces `IsChartUniv` — antecedent 1 of
15	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — to `IsChartLocusFibre`.  **That reduction passes through the
16	unrestricted certificate, which the project's headers assert to be false**, and this file is
17	the repair.

19	## The defect, measured
20	
21	`IsChartLocusFibre` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:152`) asks for a
22	`ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart …) g` at every test — the datum for the *unrestricted*
23	chart, with `W` a free structure field.  Nothing pins `W := chartLocus`, although the docstring
24	there says the `W` field "is already discharged — it is `chartLocus`".  So the open `V` never
25	enters the hypothesis, and one term gives back the unrestricted certificate:
26	
27	```
28	isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some
29	  : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)
30	```
31	
32	That measurement is **not** repeated here: it is landed as
33	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` and
34	`mono_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` in `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean`, together
35	with `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` — the criterion's own emptiness guard, finally
36	instantiated at the Abel chart.  In `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` the restriction to `V` is
37	applied *after* the unrestricted certificate is in hand, so restricting buys nothing on the way
38	in.
39	
40	**The precise status of "false".**  `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
41	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` all assert that the Abel chart is not injective (the
42	linear system `|D|`), and by the guard above that assertion makes `IsChartLocusFibre`
43	unsatisfiable.  But **no declaration proves the non-injectivity**: the guard takes
44	`¬ Function.Injective` as a hypothesis.  So `IsChartLocusFibre` is *conditionally* unsatisfiable
45	— dead if the headers are right, and nobody has shown they are.  This file therefore does not
46	claim the old route is dead; it claims the old route is gated on a proposition the project
47	believes false and has never checked, which is reason enough not to build on it.
48	
49	The criterion itself is **not** at fault: it is stated for an arbitrary morphism of presheaves
50	and is correct.  What was wrong is the *instantiation* — at `abelSigmaChart` rather than at
51	`restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) V`.
52	
53	## What this file provides
54	
55	* `RestrictedChartFibre` — the same datum demanded at the **restricted** chart, so
56	  `exists_factor` only has to factor test points *of `V`*.
57	* `isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre` — it gives `IsChartUniv` at that same `V`, one
58	  application of the existing criterion, with no unrestricted certificate in between.

60	  datum still forces injectivity of the restricted chart on every test.
61	* `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` — **the `V`-coupled assembly** (inbox `I-0861`):
62	  per-index restricted fibre data on the `hf` side, and on the coverage side the containment
63	  hypothesis `hV` of `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.liftPointwiseToOpens`, together give the
64	  representation.  The two sides are made to share the same `V` by typing.
65	
66	## Division of labour with the two sibling files landed the same round
67	
68	`Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean` records why the *old* route must not be used, and
69	`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` supplies the **coverage** half of the `V`-coupling
70	(`liftPointwiseToOpens`, and the converse `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` showing `hV` is
71	exactly the gap).  This file supplies the **`hf`** half — the fibre datum at the restricted
72	chart — and the assembly that consumes both.  Nothing here re-proves either sibling.
73	
74	## The honest limits, stated rather than left for a reviewer
75	
76	* **Nothing here produces any input.**  This file replaces a badly-gated route by a
77	  well-gated one; it discharges no antecedent.  `rep` (divisor representability) is a hypothesis
78	  throughout, and `IsChartUniv` is not even statable without it.
79	* **`RestrictedChartFibre` at `V = ⊥` is expected to be cheap, and that is NOT verified here.**
80	  The injectivity content plainly degenerates at `V = ⊥` (no nonempty test has a point of the
81	  empty open subscheme — the shape `I-0861` measured for `hf`), so this class is *not* a

9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/

9	# THE PRODUCER: `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` for a class in the image of the sheafification unit
10	
11	## What this file closes
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
14	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:
15	
16	> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
17	> nothing here produces such a datum.
18	
19	**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
20	sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
21	**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
22	`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
23	so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
24	on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
25	`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
26	it they are the same class.
27	
28	## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction
29	
30	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
32	plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
33	from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.
34	
35	That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
36	automatic:
37	
38	* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
39	  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
40	  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
41	* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
42	  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
43	  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
44	  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.
45	
46	  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
47	  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
48	  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
49	  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
50	  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
51	  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
52	  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.
53	
54	  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
55	  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
56	  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,
57	  honesty of a chart value reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` alone — so `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` was
58	  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
59	  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
60	  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.
61

66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt` — the producer, with the datum given.

262	/-- **THE ABEL VALUE IS HONEST AT EVERY TEST** — the witness that carries weight, and the one this
263	file's header cited by name before it existed (see the header's own retraction).
264	
265	The θ- and Σ-family witnesses above are the *twist factors*, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest`
266	discharges anyway; they say nothing about the class being charted.  Since
267	`chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` and honesty is a subgroup condition, honesty of a **chart
268	value** reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` — so this is the row that makes CHART-U(b) unconditional
269	on the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart actually reads.
270	
271	It is cheap for a structural reason: `abelDiv`'s components are `abelDivPlus`, i.e. `PicEtAff.unit`
272	of `relPicMk` of the family's class, and `relPicToPicEt`'s components are `PicEtAff.unit` of
273	`relPicMap` — so the witness on the piece `U` is the class of the *restricted* family, and
274	`abelDiv_val` plus `picEtMap_abelDiv` line the two up. -/
275	theorem abelDiv_isPlusHonest {n : ℕ} (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
276	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
277	    IsPlusHonest C T (abelDiv C π n T s) := by
278	  intro U
279	  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1))
280	    ((divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n Γ(T.left, U.1)
281	      (divFamZar.map C π n (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) s)).picClass), ?_⟩
282	  rw [picEtMap_abelDiv, abelDiv_overSpec]
283	  rfl
284	
285	variable (C) in
286	/-- **`chartTwist` PRESERVES honesty** — the reason the producer reaches the Σ-chart.
287	
288	`chartTwist λ = λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`, and both twist factors are θ-families, hence honest at every test
289	with no hypothesis.  Since honesty is a subgroup condition, the twisted class is honest exactly
290	when `λ` is.
291	
292	So the residue of CHART-U(b) is **the λ-factor alone**: no twist bookkeeping enters, which is the
293	mis-pricing the §3.3 correction 5 records. -/
294	theorem chartTwist_isPlusHonest (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
295	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
296	    IsPlusHonest C T (chartTwist C m Z T lam) := by
297	  rw [chartTwist]
298	  exact (hlam.mul C ((thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C (thetaCechClass C) T).pow C m)).mul C
299	    ((sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest C Z T).inv C)
300	
301	/-! ## CHART-U(b) with the residue discharged -/
302	
303	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
304	variable (C π) in
305	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST, WITH NO RESIDUE**, for a class that is honest on the affine
306	pieces of the test.
307	
308	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` needs a per-piece datum with the plus-class property;
309	`exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` produces one from honesty, and
310	`chartTwist_isPlusHonest` says the twist does not disturb honesty.  So the whole chain — the
311	engine, RE-5, the dictionary, the fibre-field invariance, `haff`, the presentation, `hconv`,
312	`hplus`, and now the producer — closes on the single hypothesis `IsPlusHonest`.
313	
314	`IsAffineHom π` follows from `IsFinite π`, whence the disabled overlapping-instance linter — the
315	same configuration `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_plusFibre` carries and for the same reason. -/
316	theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest
317	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
318	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
319	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
320	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) :=
321	  isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre C π hπ m Z T lam fun U =>
322	    exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range C π _
323	      (by
324	        obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := chartTwist_isPlusHonest C m Z T hlam U
325	        exact ⟨z, hz.trans (picEtMap_chartTwist m Z (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)⟩)
326	
327	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
328	variable (C π) in
329	/-- **The chart locus as an OPEN OF THE TEST, from honesty alone** — the shape the `W` field of a
330	chart datum consumes (`chartLocusOpens`, `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:115`), with its `haff`
331	argument discharged rather than passed through.
332	
333	This is c9b's clause (i) paid in full for an honest class: not "reduced to", but produced. -/
334	def chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
335	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
336	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
337	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
338	    T.left.Opens where
339	  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
340	  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam
341	
342	@[simp]
343	lemma mem_chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
344	    {hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom}
345	    {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
346	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} {hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam}
347	    {t : T.left} :
348	    t ∈ chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
349	  Iff.rfl
350	
351	end

9	/-!
10	# The coupling of the atlas open to the coverage witness
11	
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) has three antecedents, and
13	the board tracks them on three separate rows: `IsChartUniv` (c9b), Zariski-local surjectivity
14	of `Sigma.desc f` (dat-b B-6), and `rep i` (divrep).  Reading those rows one concludes the
15	three compose — discharge each and the seam fires.
16	
17	**They do not compose as stated.**  The atlas the seam consumes is a family of *restricted*
18	charts `restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) (V i)` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:86`),
19	whose source is `(V i : Scheme)` — an open of the *chart source*, i.e. of the divisor scheme.
20	So the coverage antecedent, unfolded through `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
21	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), must produce a chart point
22	`x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ (V i : Scheme)` landing **in that same `V i`**, while coverage geometry
23	produces a point of the divisor scheme `D.left` with no such constraint.  The two opens the
24	route wants to identify live on different objects — `V i` on the divisor scheme, `chartLocus`
25	on the test — and no declaration in the tree relates them.
26	
27	That is an obligation *between* two antecedents, owned by no row, and it is why "close c9b,
28	then close B-6" would not have composed even with both closed.
29	
30	## What this file does about it
31	
32	It names the coupling and derives restricted coverage from unrestricted coverage together
33	with a range containment: the coverage witness, viewed in the chart source, factors
34	set-theoretically through `V i`.  Given that, the witness lifts to `V i` along the open
35	immersion `(V i).ι` by `IsOpenImmersion.lift`, and the class it names is unchanged because
36	`restrictChart` is *by definition* precomposition with `yoneda.map (V i).ι` — so the lift's
37	chart value is the unlifted one, with no transport.
38	
39	**THREE CORRECTIONS TO AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS HEADER**, all from a fresh-context audit
40	(2026-07-29, inbox `I-0894`), because each would have mispriced the row:
41	
42	1. the hypothesis is **NOT "weaker than either antecedent"**, as the draft claimed.  It is the
43	   unrestricted coverage datum **conjoined** with the containment, so it *implies* the
44	   coverage antecedent and is strictly STRONGER than it.  What is true is the much smaller
45	   claim that the containment is all that separates unrestricted from restricted coverage;
46	2. `liftPointwiseToOpens` and `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` together are one
47	   **biconditional**, and its transport step (`restrictChart_app_apply`) is `rfl`.  So this
48	   file is a *repackaging with its difference named*, and **it closes no gate**.  It is
49	   reported as routing information, not as progress on any antecedent;
50	3. the draft argued about "`V i = chartLocus`" in two places.  **Those carriers do not meet**:
51	   `V i : (X i).Opens` is an open of the chart source (the divisor scheme), while
52	   `chartLocus C m Z lam : Set ↥T.left` is a set on a *test*.  The only bridge is
53	   `chartLocusOpens`, which lands in `T.left.Opens` and costs `haff` (= dat-b's B-4).  The
54	   mismatch is precisely what this file was written to expose, so reasoning as though the two
55	   were interchangeable — as the draft did below — defeated the purpose.
56	
57	What survives all three: the containment is genuine content (probes below), it is exactly the
58	difference between the two coverage statements (the converse), and no declaration in the tree
59	relates the two carriers.
60	
61	## Main declarations
62	
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseCoverage` — the pointwise coverage datum of B-5, named for an
64	  arbitrary chart family so the two atlases (unrestricted, restricted) can be compared.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.liftPointwiseToOpens` — **the coupling**: pointwise coverage for a family
66	  `f` plus the range containment gives pointwise coverage for the *restricted* family
67	  `fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)`.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise` — the composite into the
69	  instance the seam consumes, for the restricted atlas.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` — the **converse**: restricted
71	  coverage gives unrestricted coverage *and* the containment.  So `hV` is not a hypothesis
72	  chosen for provability — it is exactly the difference between the two, and a lane cannot
73	  reach the restricted atlas while avoiding it.
74	-/

76	set_option autoImplicit false
77	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

79	universe u
80	
81	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
82	
83	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
84	
85	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
86	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
87	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
88	
89	noncomputable section
90	
91	variable (C) in
92	/-- **The pointwise coverage datum of B-5**, named.
93	
94	This is verbatim the hypothesis of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
95	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), given a name so that the same statement can be
96	compared at two different chart families — which is the whole point of this file: B-6 is
97	consumed at the *restricted* atlas, while coverage geometry produces the datum at the
98	*unrestricted* one. -/
99	def PointwiseCoverage {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
100	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
101	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
102	    ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
103	      (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s
104	
105	/-! ## The chart value of a restricted chart at a lifted point -/
106	
107	/-- **A restricted chart reads a lifted point exactly as the unrestricted chart reads the
108	point itself.**
109	
110	`restrictChart f V` is `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f` by definition, so its value at `u` is the value
111	of `f` at `u ≫ V.ι`.  No transport, no naturality of `f` — the composition is on the source
112	side, where `yoneda.map` is precomposition.
113	
114	This is the entire reason the coupling below is cheap, and it is worth isolating: a lane that
115	expected the two chart values to differ by a restriction map would look for a compatibility
116	that is not needed. -/
117	lemma restrictChart_app_apply {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
118	    (V : X.Opens) {S : Scheme.{u}} (u : S ⟶ (V : Scheme.{u})) :
119	    (restrictChart f V).app (op S) u = f.app (op S) (u ≫ V.ι) :=
120	  rfl
121	
122	/-! ## The coupling -/
123	
124	variable (C) in
125	/-- **THE COUPLING**: pointwise coverage for `f` plus a range containment gives pointwise
126	coverage for the restricted family.
127	
128	The containment is the honest content: at the point, index and witness coverage produces, the
129	witness's image in the chart source lies inside `V i`.  Everything else is the lift along the
130	open immersion `(V i).ι` and `restrictChart_app_apply`, which is `rfl` — so this direction
131	carries no mathematics beyond the lift, and together with its converse below it is a
132	biconditional rather than a reduction.  **It closes no gate.**
133	
134	Note the shape of the hypothesis: it quantifies over the data coverage *returns*, not over all
135	opens or all witnesses.  So a producer discharges it exactly where it produces the witness,
136	which is the only place the information is available; a formulation asking for the containment
137	uniformly over all witnesses would be strictly stronger.
138	
139	What the containment *means* geometrically depends on which open `V i` is, and this file
140	deliberately does not assume an answer — in particular `V i` is an open of the chart source
141	while `chartLocus` is a set on a test, so the two are not interchangeable and the intended
142	instantiation still owes the `chartLocusOpens` bridge (cost: `haff`, i.e. dat-b's B-4). -/
143	theorem liftPointwiseToOpens {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
144	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
145	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
146	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
147	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
148	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
149	    PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)) := by
150	  intro T s t
151	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, x, hx, hrange⟩ := h T s t
152	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, IsOpenImmersion.lift ((V i).ι) x hrange, ?_⟩
153	  rw [restrictChart_app_apply, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]
154	  exact hx
155	
156	variable (C) in
157	/-- **The composite**: coverage plus the containment gives the local-surjectivity instance
158	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes *at the restricted atlas* — which is the atlas
159	`mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) and every real chart family
160	is built from.
161	
162	Stated because this, not `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise`, is what a coverage lane
163	owes when the atlas is restricted: the two differ by exactly `hV`. -/
164	theorem isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
165	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
166	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
167	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
168	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
169	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
170	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
171	      (Sigma.desc (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :=
172	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ (liftPointwiseToOpens C f V h)
173	
174	/-! ## The converse: `hV` is the exact difference, not a convenient extra
175	
176	A coupling lemma whose hypothesis is stronger than the gap it bridges hides the gap instead of
177	naming it.  This section rules that out: restricted coverage gives back unrestricted coverage
178	together with the containment, so `hV` is precisely what separates the two. -/
179	
180	variable (C) in
181	/-- **The converse of the coupling.**  Pointwise coverage for the restricted family gives
182	pointwise coverage for `f` *and* the range containment at the produced witness.
183	
184	So `liftPointwiseToOpens`' hypothesis is not a strengthening chosen to make the proof go: it
185	is logically equivalent to the conclusion.  In particular a lane cannot obtain B-6 for the
186	restricted atlas — the one the seam consumes — while avoiding the statement that coverage hits
187	its classes inside `V i`.
188	
189	The witness is `x ≫ (V i).ι`, whose range is contained in that of `(V i).ι` by construction,
190	and whose chart value under `f i` is the restricted chart's value at `x` by
191	`restrictChart_app_apply`. -/
192	theorem pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
193	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
194	    (h : PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :
195	    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
196	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
197	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
198	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base) := by
199	  intro T s t
200	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, u, hu⟩ := h T s t
201	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, u ≫ (V i).ι, hu, ?_⟩
202	  intro z hz
203	  obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := hz
204	  exact ⟨u.base w, rfl⟩
205	
206	end
207	
208	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49

51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/

77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83	
84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)

97	/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i

114	variable (C π) in
115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.
121	
122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139

82	one deliberate design choice: the sieve is described through the individual `f i`, so a
83	producer discharges it by exhibiting, for each point of `T`, one open neighbourhood and one
84	index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
85	that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/
86	def ChartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
